requirements.quote:
This message can be sent
   by either peer after it has sent a Finished message.
requirements.required_behavior: send KeyUpdate only after that endpoint has sent Finished
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's KeyUpdate position can be compared with its Finished message.

requirements.quote:
Implementations
   that receive a KeyUpdate message prior to receiving a Finished
   message MUST terminate the connection with an "unexpected_message"
   alert.
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives KeyUpdate before receiving the peer's Finished
requirements.forbidden_behavior: processing the premature KeyUpdate or continuing the connection
requirements.why_checkable: A premature KeyUpdate has an exact terminal alert outcome.

requirements.quote:
After sending a KeyUpdate message, the sender SHALL send all
   its traffic using the next generation of keys
requirements.required_behavior: use the next generation of sending keys for all subsequent traffic
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending subsequent traffic with the previous generation
requirements.why_checkable: The key-generation transition can be correlated with the KeyUpdate record.

requirements.quote:
the next generation of keys, computed as described
   in Section 7.2.
requirements.required_behavior: compute the next key generation using the Section 7.2 traffic-secret update
requirements.why_checkable: The derivation routine and its inputs can be compared with the referenced key schedule.

requirements.quote:
Upon receiving a KeyUpdate, the receiver MUST update
   its receiving keys.
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives a valid KeyUpdate
requirements.required_behavior: advance its receiving keys to the next generation
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continuing to use the old receiving generation for subsequent peer traffic
requirements.why_checkable: The receive-key state transition follows a specific handshake message.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: using another numeric value for update_not_requested
requirements.why_checkable: The enum's wire value is explicit.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: using another numeric value for update_requested
requirements.why_checkable: The enum's wire value is explicit.

requirements.condition: encoding or parsing a KeyUpdate message
requirements.required_behavior: encode exactly one request_update field of type KeyUpdateRequest
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omitting request_update or adding other message fields
requirements.why_checkable: The complete handshake body structure is explicit.

requirements.quote:
If an implementation
      receives any other value, it MUST terminate the connection with an
      "illegal_parameter" alert.
requirements.condition: request_update has a value other than 0 or 1
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accepting or ignoring the unknown value
requirements.why_checkable: Every invalid byte value has one specified alert outcome.

requirements.quote:
If the request_update field is set to "update_requested", then the
   receiver MUST send a KeyUpdate of its own
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives KeyUpdate with request_update equal to update_requested
requirements.why_checkable: A request value of 1 can be matched to the peer's response trace.

requirements.quote:
the
   receiver MUST send a KeyUpdate of its own with request_update set to
   "update_not_requested"
requirements.condition: an endpoint responds to KeyUpdate with update_requested
requirements.required_behavior: set request_update in the responding KeyUpdate to update_not_requested
requirements.forbidden_behavior: setting update_requested in the mandatory response
requirements.why_checkable: The response field has a fixed required enum value.

requirements.quote:
the
   receiver MUST send a KeyUpdate of its own with request_update set to
   "update_not_requested" prior to sending its next Application Data
   record.
requirements.condition: an endpoint owes a KeyUpdate response
requirements.required_behavior: send the responding KeyUpdate before its next Application Data record
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending Application Data before the response KeyUpdate
requirements.why_checkable: The two outbound record types have a strict ordering requirement.

requirements.quote:
This mechanism allows either side to force an update to the
   entire connection, but causes an implementation which receives



Rescorla                     Standards Track                   [Page 76]

RFC 8446                           TLS                       August 2018


   multiple KeyUpdates while it is silent to respond with a single
   update.
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives multiple KeyUpdates requesting an update before it sends its response
requirements.required_behavior: coalesce the pending requests into a single responding KeyUpdate
requirements.forbidden_behavior: sending one response for every queued request
requirements.why_checkable: A burst of request messages can verify the number of emitted responses.

requirements.quote:
If implementations independently send their own KeyUpdates with
   request_update set to "update_requested" and they cross in flight,
   then each side will also send a response
requirements.condition: both endpoints' update_requested KeyUpdates cross in flight
requirements.required_behavior: each endpoint also send one responding KeyUpdate
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treating the crossed request as satisfying the required response
requirements.why_checkable: A controlled crossed-flight trace can verify both response messages.

requirements.quote:
If implementations independently send their own KeyUpdates with
   request_update set to "update_requested" and they cross in flight,
   then each side will also send a response, with the result that each
   side increments by two generations.
requirements.condition: both endpoints' update_requested KeyUpdates cross in flight
requirements.required_behavior: advance each sending and receiving direction by the two resulting key generations
requirements.forbidden_behavior: advancing only one generation for the crossed request and response
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent traffic can be tested against the expected generation count.

requirements.quote:
Both sender and receiver MUST encrypt their KeyUpdate messages with
   the old keys.
requirements.condition: an endpoint sends an initiating KeyUpdate
requirements.required_behavior: encrypt the KeyUpdate with the current pre-update sending keys
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encrypting the KeyUpdate with the newly derived keys
requirements.why_checkable: Decryptability under the old versus new traffic key is deterministic.

requirements.quote:
Both sender and receiver MUST encrypt their KeyUpdate messages with
   the old keys.
requirements.condition: an endpoint sends a KeyUpdate response
requirements.required_behavior: encrypt the response KeyUpdate with its current pre-update sending keys
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encrypting the response with the next-generation keys
requirements.why_checkable: The response record's protection generation can be tested directly.

requirements.quote:
Additionally, both sides MUST enforce that a KeyUpdate
   with the old key is received before accepting any messages encrypted
   with the new key.
requirements.condition: an endpoint receives traffic protected with a peer's next-generation key
requirements.required_behavior: accept it only after receiving that peer's KeyUpdate under the old key
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accepting new-key traffic before the old-key KeyUpdate
requirements.why_checkable: Reordered records can test the exact key-transition gate.
